```{r}
orders <- read.csv("olist_orders_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
order_reviews <- read.csv("olist_order_reviews_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
customers <- read.csv("olist_customers_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
order_items <- read.csv("olist_order_items_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))

```

```{r}
names(orders)
names(order_reviews)

```

```{r}
str(orders)
```

```{r}
class(orders$order_purchase_timestamp)
class(orders$order_delivered_customer_date)
class(orders$order_estimated_delivery_date)
```
Since the dates in the orders data are characters and we need them as dates, we convert them
```{r}
orders <- orders %>%
  mutate(
    order_purchase_timestamp = 
      as.POSIXct(order_purchase_timestamp,
      format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),

    order_approved_at =
      as.POSIXct(order_approved_at,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    
    order_delivered_carrier_date =
      as.POSIXct(order_delivered_carrier_date,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    
    order_delivered_customer_date =
      as.POSIXct(order_delivered_customer_date,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),

    order_estimated_delivery_date =
      as.POSIXct(order_estimated_delivery_date,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")    
  )
```

```{r}
head(orders)
```

find missing values
```{r}
colSums(is.na(orders))
colSums(is.na(order_reviews))
colSums(is.na(customers))
colSums(is.na(order_items))
colSums(is.na(sellers))
colSums(is.na(products))
colSums(is.na(product_name_trans))
```

Check by delivery status
```{r}
orders |> 
  filter(is.na(order_delivered_customer_date)) |> 
  count(order_status)
```

Check duplicates and IDs
```{r}
sum(duplicated(orders))
sum(duplicated(order_reviews))
sum(duplicated(customers))
sum(duplicated(order_items))
sum(duplicated(sellers))
sum(duplicated(products))
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_id) |> 
  filter(n > 1)
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_id) |> 
  summarise(
    orders = n(),
    duplicated_orders = sum(n > 1)
  )
```
So one row is one order as we expect

Check Customers

```{r}
customers |> 
  count(customer_id) |> 
  filter(n > 1)
```

```{r}
n_distinct(customers$customer_id)
n_distinct(customers$customer_unique_id)
```
Meaning that a person can have multiple orders, but most have just one.

Check order items
```{r}
order_items |> 
  count(order_id) |> 
  summarise(
    orders = n(),
    orders_with_multiple_items = sum(n > 1)
  )
```
Check reviews
```{r}
order_reviews |> 
  count(order_id) |> 
  count(n, name = "number_of_orders")
```
```{r}
order_reviews |> 
  count(order_id) |> 
  filter(n > 1)
```
So orders can have more than one review
Check categorial variables
```{r}
count(orders, order_status)
count(customers, customer_state, sort = TRUE)
count(products, product_category_name, sort = TRUE)
```
# Analysis

Check order status and how many orders were delivered

```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_status) |> 
  mutate(
    percentage = n / sum(n)
  )
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_status) |> 
  mutate(order_status = fct_reorder(order_status, n)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = order_status, y = n, fill = order_status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = comma(n)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "red4"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,    
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Number of orders by order status",
    subtitle = "Sorted from most to least common",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of orders"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15))
```
Check delivery rate

```{r}
orders |> 
  summarise(
    total_orders = n(),
    delivered_orders = sum(order_status == "delivered"),
    non_delivered_orders = sum(order_status != "delivered"),
    delivered_share = mean(order_status == "delivered")
  )
```
Check dates
```{r}
orders |> 
  summarise(
    earliest_purchase = min(order_purchase_timestamp, na.rm = TRUE),
    latest_purchase = max(order_purchase_timestamp, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  summarise(
    earliest_delivery = min(order_delivered_customer_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    latest_delivery = max(order_delivered_customer_date, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

Check for impossible sequences
```{r}
orders |> 
  filter(
    order_delivered_customer_date < order_purchase_timestamp
  )
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  filter(
    order_delivered_customer_date <
      order_approved_at
  )
```
So a bit weird with these 61 orders that were delivered before they were approved.

Examine the time period
```{r}
orders <- orders |> 
  mutate(
    purchase_month = floor_date(
      order_purchase_timestamp,
      unit = "month"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
ordersorders |> 
  count(purchase_month)
```
```{r}
head(orders)
```
```{r}
orders_monthly <- orders |>  count(purchase_month)
```


```{r}
peak <- orders_monthly %>% filter(n == max(n))

ggplot(orders_monthly, aes(x = purchase_month, y = n)) +
  geom_area(fill = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(color = "#2A9D8F", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(data = peak, color = "#E76F51", size = 5) +
  geom_label(
    data = peak,
    aes(label = paste0("Peak: ", comma(n))),
    color = "#E76F51",
    fontface = "bold",
    vjust = -0.8,
    linewidth = 0,
    fill = "white"
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of orders over time",
    subtitle = "Monthly order volume, with the busiest month highlighted",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of orders"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
  )
```
